subject: psychiatry
title: Perinatal, geriatric and culture-bound conditions in psychiatry

steps.tx: In **postpartum psychosis**, delusions often centre on the baby, such as the belief that the child is dead or malformed. Risk is higher in primigravidae. Before labelling it psychiatric, exclude organic causes such as **cortical vein thrombosis** and **Sheehan syndrome**, which are important mimics after delivery.

steps.tx: Geriatric psychiatry commonly encounters **dementia**, **depression**, alcoholism and paranoia. Depression can be secondary to medical disease, including **Cushing syndrome**, Addison disease, hypothyroidism, stroke and Parkinson disease. Stroke location matters: left anterior lesions tend to cause depression, while right posterior lesions tend to cause anosognosia.

steps.tx: Abnormal grief can become **morbid grief** when symptoms persist beyond six months. Sensing the deceased's presence and hearing their voice may occur. Where auditory hallucinations and anxiety dominate, an antipsychotic such as **haloperidol** is used. Consultation-liaison psychiatry addresses psychiatric illness in medically ill patients.

steps.tx: Culture-bound syndromes are seen in particular communities. **Koro** is the fear that the penis is retracting into the body and will cause death. **Dhat syndrome** is seen in parts of the Indian subcontinent, where the patient believes semen is lost in urine, causing weakness. **Latah** involves startle, echolalia and echopraxia, while **amok** is sudden violent rage.
